method: SYNTHETIC TEST DATA — no soil map, pollen record or rule engine was consulted. Classes are derived by app/scripts/make-test-dem.mjs from the fixture's own closed-form terrain and its §7 connectivity grid, for the single reference century 500 CE at the 4.35 m level its synthetic shoreline table gives at that year. It exists so the app's Phase-7 land-cover feature can be exercised end to end against app/public/data/testsite/ without the Python pipeline. A real site derives its classes from SGU Jordarter plus the DEM.
caveat: Synthetic test data — a rule model of one century, not a survey of past vegetation. (A real site states the rule engine's own caveat here.)
calibration: SYNTHETIC TEST DATA — not calibrated against anything. The forest/open split here is whatever the closed-form hill produces; a real site reports its forest/open ratio against the regional pollen literature (PLAN §2.5).

classes.name: Water (sea, ~500 CE)
classes.rule: Sea-connectivity value at or below the 4.3 m reference water level (connect ≤ level, docs/data-formats.md §7) — wet AND connected to the open sea, so enclosed basins below that level are excluded.

classes.name: Reed bed and shore fen
classes.rule: Dry at the reference level but flooded by a further 1.2 m rise (connect ≤ 5.5 m): the shallow, seasonally wet shore band.

classes.name: Damp broadleaf woodland
classes.rule: Dry ground less than 4 m above the reference level (below 8.3 m), outside the fort's cleared crown — the valley floors and the enclosed basin.

classes.name: Conifer forest
classes.rule: Ground at least 4 m above the reference level whose DEM slope is at least 5 % — the hill flanks, the rampart ring and the basin rim.

classes.name: Open grazed ground
classes.rule: Everything else: gentle high ground below 5 % slope, plus a 58 m cleared radius around the fort itself.
